A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OV-AVEL work. Their complete main texts, tables, equations, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on OV-AVEBench and AVE, including baseline performance, ablations, class-wise results, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for four adapted comparison methods on OV-AVEBench.

M1.justification: The two proposed baselines retain the same frozen ImageBind encoders, similarity-based classification, temporal Transformer layers, geometric-mean fusion, and cross-entropy training. The additional adapted methods serve as comparators.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same OV-AVEBench coverage: 24,800 videos, 67 classes, and 46 seen versus 21 unseen classes. The supplementary zero-shot and fine-tuning evaluations on AVE are also retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 adds adapted CMRA, AVE, PSP, and MM-Pyramid methods, substantially expanding comparison coverage to prior fine-tuning approaches. Video-LLaMA2 and CLIP&CLAP were already evaluated in v1 Table 9 and Appendix B/Table 11, respectively.

E3.justification: The reported splits, one-second segmentation, evaluation metrics, and event-level IoU threshold remain unchanged. Section 4.1 retains ImageBind Huge, batch size 32, five fine-tuning epochs, and Adam with learning rate 5e-5; no separate revision to the evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The layer-count, background-text, fusion-strategy, temporal-versus-linear, intra-versus-cross-modal, and training-data-ratio analyses retain their results. Layer-count and intra/cross-modal studies move to v2 Appendix A and C. Class-wise analyses and qualitative examples are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. Tables and figures continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds substantial comparative results for four adapted methods across seen, unseen, and total test data. For example, MM-Pyramid achieves 68.6 seen-class average and 29.9 unseen-class average, versus the proposed fine-tuning baseline's retained 62.9 and 55.8. Existing baseline, ablation, AVE, and qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, mathematical definitions, and similarity and fusion equations are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the OV-AVEL task, OV-AVEBench, evaluation metrics, and two baselines. The additional comparisons support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly interprets the adapted-method results as showing that sophisticated fusion can improve seen-class recognition while worsening unseen-class generalization. The training-data discussion replaces v1's conjecture about more data causing overfitting with an interpretation emphasizing the nonlinear relationship between data quantity and performance.

D1.justification: v2 Section 4.2 explains how the new comparators are adapted by replacing the proposed temporal layers with their core audio-visual fusion modules. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information, Video-LLaMA2 prompts, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: The introductory literature overview adds works such as Tri-Ergon, TAVG-Bench, and open-vocabulary audio-visual semantic segmentation while removing several speech recognition and separation references. The new comparisons sharpen positioning against closed-set AVEL methods, while the central novelty framing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is reorganized into training-free, fine-tuning, and between-baseline comparisons. Former further-discussion material is redistributed, two ablation discussions move to the appendix, and affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 becomes a full-width comparative table incorporating existing comparisons and the four new methods. Several existing tables are relocated or renumbered, including two moved to the appendix. All six figure graphics remain identical, with appendix figure labels updated.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked comparisons between its fine-tuning baseline and adapted prior AVEL methods. v2 Table 2 supplies these comparisons and exposes meaningful differences between seen-class performance and unseen-class generalization, improving the benchmark's usefulness. The consolidated presentation helps assess these trade-offs, although implementation details for the new adaptations remain brief.
